q: A ball of diameter $5.0\ \text{cm}$ is dropped from rest at $t = 0$. It blocks a light gate from $t = 0.10\ \text{s}$ to $t = 0.14\ \text{s}$. What value of $g$ (in $\text{m s}^{-2}$) do these measurements give?

lines.say: A ball is dropped through a light gate, {drop}and here's what the gate records. What value of g does this give?
This is a real OCR A-level question. Pause and have a go!
Okay! {dt}The beam is blocked from nought point one oh seconds to nought point one four. That's nought point oh four seconds.
In that time, the ball moves {d}its own diameter, five centimetres. {v}So its average speed is one point two five metres per second.
Here's the key idea. {vt}With constant acceleration, speed rises in a straight line, {mid}so the average speed equals the speed halfway through the time, at nought point one two seconds.
It started from rest, {g}so g is one point two five over nought point one two. {ans}Ten point four! It's C.
{t1}Eight point nine three uses nought point one four, {t2}and twelve point five uses nought point one oh. {t3}Nine point eight one is just the textbook value!
